proves: An increment becomes a decrement, a negation loses its !, and a unary minus is removed. A test that checks a result only against zero misses the lost minus. A boolean operand in parentheses keeps the position of the operand without them, so the target of an assignment and the operands of & and ! have no negation.
fixture: negate returns -x, flip returns !ok, and count increments n. The test of negate checks only that the result is not zero. toggle reads *b, sets (*b) to true and returns !(was). address returns &(ok).
